name: Mono-safe width tricks: a 100%-wet short room IR as a stealth widener with width trim and gain make-up, a drawn and smoothed auto-pan rhythm, and Haas kept ≤15 ms split across bands tilted in opposite directions
goal: Widen one headline element so it still works in mono. (1) Stealth IR widener: convolution with a short, thin-room impulse at 100% wet and decay down to ~20% so there is no audible tail. It widens and re-colours the chords. Because width makes the part quieter in mono, trim stereo width to ~65% and add ~+6.5 dB to match levels instead of lowering the mix. (2) Rhythmic auto-pan: start ~50% amount, then draw a stepped pan curve that fits the arp, round it with smoothing, optionally switch to unsynced Hz set by ear, and add a touch of multiband treble reverb before the panner. (3) Haas without the lopsided, phasey mono sum: keep the L/R delay ≤15 ms, tune it while listening in mono, tilt a mid band to one side and the treble band to the other, then reduce width and re-level. Use it on incidental FX rather than lead vocals. Use width with restraint so the one wide element stands out. Delta vs our Haas/phase-offset, high-band pan and asymmetric L/R skills: the IR widener with width trim, drawn pan rhythm, and opposite-tilt multiband Haas.

source.title: 3 Stereo Width Tricks (That Sound Great In Mono)
source.transcript_note: Vendor-sponsored tutorial; plugin names mapped to generic convolution/width/pan modules; demo links dropped.

prerequisites: Convolution reverb with short room IRs (Web Audio: ConvolverNode with a short stereo IR, implementation note)
Auto-pan / drawable pan LFO; multiband splitter; short L/R delay

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Synth chords, arp or incidental FX to widen

outputs.name: wide_mono_safe_part
outputs.description: Wider element that keeps level and solidity in mono

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Always check in mono: width makes a part relatively quieter in mono, so trim width and make up gain.
Haas >~40 ms is heard as a separate echo; <~40 ms fuses into width, and ≤15 ms reduces mono phasing.
Use one standout wide element; if everything is wide, nothing feels wide.
Source is a vendor tutorial; techniques are mapped to generic devices.

steps.action: Insert convolution reverb on the chords at 100% wet with a short, thin room IR and decay reduced to ~20% so no tail is heard. Audition other short IRs for different timbres.
steps.expect: Chords sound similar but wider and re-coloured, not reverberant

steps.action: Sum to mono: the widened chords drop in level. Instead of lowering the wet mix, follow with a width control at ~65% and raise gain ~6.5 dB to level-match.
steps.expect: Wide in stereo, balanced in mono, wrapping around a mono bass

steps.action: Rhythmic pan for arps/synths: auto-pan at ~50% amount, try LFO shapes, then draw a custom stepped pan curve and add smoothing to round its edges. Optionally switch rate to unsynced Hz and set by ear to fit the part.
steps.expect: Part bounces between speakers yet stays centred in mono

steps.action: Add a touch of multiband treble-only reverb before the panner for air; adjust pan mix lower for just a flutter, or full for strong L/R jumps.
steps.expect: Airy top end without washing the lows

steps.action: Haas: duplicate L/R with a delay on one side. Keep it at ≤15 ms and tune it while listening in mono until acceptable.
Fix the lopsided tilt: split into bands, tilt the mid band to the right and the treble band to the left, then reduce width and re-level.
steps.expect: Wide, balanced image that is acceptable in mono

steps.action: Apply these to one headline sound (incidental FX/ear candy for Haas) while keeping most of the mix centred.
steps.expect: Contrast makes the wide element pop in mono and stereo

verification: Mono sum of the IR-widened chords is level-matched to bypass within ~1 dB.
Auto-panned arp remains audible and solid in mono.
Haas delay is ≤15 ms; the image no longer leans to one side after the multiband tilt.
Only one or two elements in the mix use these width tricks.
